newsitem.title: USA: SEC probes Jacksonville, Fla., bond issues - paper.
newsitem.headline: SEC probes Jacksonville, Fla., bond issues - paper.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission has issued subpoenaes in a probe of bonds issued by Florida's Duval County School Board the Jacksonville Electric Authority, Florida Times-Union reported Tuesday.
SEC officials were not immediately available for comment.

The newspaper said the SEC sought records detailing relationships among firms and individuals in the municipal bond industry, and bonds issued from 1991 to 1993 by the Duval County school board and the Electric Authority.
The newspaper said the SEC specifically sought:
--Records detailing Jacksonville's dealings with investment bankers Lazard, Freres and Co and William R. Hough and Co; and with the Tallahassee consulting firm Nat Cole and Associates Inc.

--Records of Electric Authority bond issues on which Lazard, Freres acted as financial adivser, including a $205.6 million bond refinancing in July 1992, a $130.6 million issue in January 1993, and a $457.5 million refinancing in March 1993.

--Records from an April 1992 school board bond refinancing of $184.5 million, including meeting agendas and notes, tape recordings, correspondence, calandar entries, phone message slips and diary enteries concerning Hough; Lazard, Freres; Cole; attorney Robert Harris and his firm; and Jacksonville printer Horace Drew.
--Electric Authority records on the selection of financial advisers from 1991 to 1993.
--Campaign records filed by school board members Stan Jordan and Billy Parker, and records of school boundray proposals and changes.
The newspaper quoted the Electric Authority's former managing director, Royce Lyles, as saying the SEC probe may be related to an investigation of Lazard Freres.
The authority terminated its contract with Lazard Freres in March 1995 because of federal investigations into the firm's activities.

Lazard Frere was one of two firms that paid a $24 milion fine in October 1995 to the SEC for failing to disclose to its clients a fee-splitting arrangement with another investment bank. In August 1996, former Lazard Freres partner Mark Ferber was convicted in a federal court in Boston of fraud for his involvement with the fee arrangement. Ferber is appealing the verdict.
